assessments.reasoning: Seven contiguous parts cover the 102,067-byte SPDX json/details record with reported SHA-256 77d2ee552d757921500b412707a348d395f4d165b8432d181e080d0a3d7cba9c. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 4 gives licenseId=LGPL-2.1-or-later and identifies the file notice as the evidence distinguishing the elections. Both the standard header and its template preserve the recipient’s option. The record cites the two GNU HTML representations and OSI’s LGPL-2.1 page. These links identify possible witnesses only.

The SPDX repository’s annotated v3.29.0 tag object points to commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the exact revision in the or-later JSON locator and proposed value. The captured tag response reports SHA-256 9695bf0c0fae8f1db7f1bee44d2176c06a045a3fb62f1ab9aa4b4cef283ebd13. The tag is unsigned and supplies release provenance only.

The pinned GNU text’s §13 and “How to Apply These Terms to Your New Libraries” are the controlling context. Section 13 describes the recipient’s election when the library specifies a version and “any later version.” The application notice instantiates that rule with 2.1. SPDX’s reproduced exhibit shares the publisher text’s lineage and adds no independent evidence about any project’s grant.

limitations: The shared documentary edition supports two conditional correspondences. The or-later option belongs to the grant described in this statement. A copy of the edition alone cannot establish that option for every file.

SPDX’s generated text uses the FSF postal address and the sample signatory Ty Coon. The inspected GNU text uses web addresses and Moe Ghoul. The version-option clause agrees across these representations despite those wording differences.

The three proposed records set revalidation for 2027-05-25T00:00:00Z, with earlier review upon a relevant publisher or SPDX correction or contrary evidence about identity, correspondence or base edition.
reasoning: SPDX 3.29.0 lists LGPL-2.1-or-later. Its standard header offers “either version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.” The FSF application example uses the same election. Section 13 identifies the eligible later versions as versions published by the Free Software Foundation. The recipient can still choose 2.1.
